title: 1 · I want, I can
intro: We'll build real sentences from two little engine words — no memorising lists. Say each answer out loud before you reveal it.

steps.teach: אני (ani) = I. רוצה (rotze) = want. Just put them side by side.
Add an infinitive straight on. לבוא (lavo) = to come.
לא (lo) = not. It sits right before the verb.
steps.answer: אני לא יכול לבוא  (ani lo yachol lavo)
אני לא רוצה לישון  (ani lo rotze lishon)

title: 2 · You, and asking
intro: Same engine, new pieces. To ask a yes/no question in Hebrew you keep the same word order and just raise your tone.

steps.teach: אתה (ata) = you (to a man). Word order stays the same to ask.
צריך (tzarich) = need / have to. ללכת (lalechet) = to go.

steps.answer: אני לא רוצה לעזור  (ani lo rotze la'azor)

title: 3 · the, and, in
intro: The smallest words in Hebrew aren't words at all — they're single letters glued to the front of the next word. Master these and whole sentences open up.

steps.teach: ב (be) glued on = "in". Before "the", be + ha fuses to "ba".
ו (ve) glued on = "and". קפה (kafe) = coffee, מים (mayim) = water.
A definite object takes את (et) in front of it.
steps.answer: אני רוצה את הקפה  (ani rotze et ha-kafe)
